inputs.label: Enhanced color
inputs.coverage: The mapping team’s published color composite assigns the p, v and ul filters to red, green and blue. It includes near-infrared light and is not natural color. Global brightness and contrast were matched across observations, so these mosaic values are unsuitable for quantitative photometry. Local residual shadows remain.

inputs.label: Equatorial close-up
inputs.coverage: Images taken by Hayabusa2 during MASCOT deployment show boulders across Ryugu’s equatorial strip. The original sampling is about 28 cm per pixel; the display is coarser. Brightness includes the illumination when the photographs were taken. The grid marks gaps and the unobserved poles.

inputs.label: Thermal inertia
inputs.coverage: False colors show how slowly the surface heats and cools, inferred from a thermal model fitted to Hayabusa2 observations. Higher values mean slower temperature changes. This is a thermal property, not a temperature map. The underlying observations sampled roughly 4.5 m per pixel; the finer map grid adds no measured detail. The grid marks missing values.

inputs.label: Spectral slope
inputs.coverage: False colors show the change in reflectance from blue to near-infrared light (b–x bands). Positive values mean a redder spectrum; negative values mean bluer. This does not measure terrain slope or identify minerals. The source’s saturated ±1 endpoints are withheld, and the grid marks those pixels. Polar mapping artifacts remain.
